name: foundry-packages
description: Workspace root. Not published — see packages/ for the published packages.

scripts.//shell: npm runs these with /bin/sh, which is dash on most Linux CI images and has no arrays and no shopt. They must be POSIX. An unmatched glob expands to the literal pattern, so `[ -d ]` on the first word is the portable way to ask whether packages/ has anything in it.
scripts.//build-order: npm --workspaces builds in filesystem-discovery order, not dependency order. Build the dependency roots first: policy feeds governance, governance feeds its deprecated compatibility packages, ui must exist before surface compiles its web templates and token consumers, and secrets has an internal subpath that must build on a fresh clone.
scripts.build: set -- packages/*/; [ -d "$1" ] || exit 0; npm run build --workspace=packages/policy --if-present && npm run build --workspace=packages/ui --if-present && npm run build --workspace=packages/secrets --if-present && npm run build --workspace=packages/governance --if-present && npm run build --workspaces --if-present
scripts.test: set -- packages/*/; [ -d "$1" ] || exit 0; npm run test --workspaces --if-present
scripts.typecheck: set -- packages/*/; [ -d "$1" ] || exit 0; npm run typecheck --workspaces --if-present
scripts.//check-registry: Does every non-private packages/*/package.json's publishConfig.registry still match the single declared registry in package-scope.json? Same single-source-of-truth pattern as check:scope, extended from the scope to the registry -- see scripts/set-registry.mjs's own header and docs/PUBLISHING.md's migration runbook.
scripts.//check-workspace-links: Does every first-party 0.x dependency range still cover its sibling's real on-disk version, and does package-lock.json still resolve every first-party package as a local link rather than a remote registry URL? See the script's own header for the defect this exists to catch -- it has already cost real time more than once.
scripts.check:gates: node scripts/test-gates.mjs && node --test scripts/agent-cloud.test.mjs scripts/deprecate-legacy-packages.test.mjs scripts/select-publishable-packages.test.mjs scripts/check-release-readiness.test.mjs scripts/check-workspace-links.test.mjs
scripts.check:readme: node scripts/check-root-readme-parity.mjs . && for manifest in packages/*/package.json; do [ -f "$manifest" ] || continue; p=${manifest%/package.json}; node scripts/check-readme-parity.mjs "$p" || exit 1; done
scripts.check:contamination: for manifest in packages/*/package.json; do [ -f "$manifest" ] || continue; p=${manifest%/package.json}; node scripts/check-contamination-classes.mjs "$p" || exit 1; done
scripts.check:typechecked-assertions: for manifest in packages/*/package.json; do [ -f "$manifest" ] || continue; p=${manifest%/package.json}; node scripts/check-typechecked-assertions.mjs "$p" || exit 1; done
scripts.//check-contrast: ui-contrast-check ships as an installed `bin` (packages/ui/src/tokens/contrast-cli.ts), but a gate nothing ever runs is decorative — invoked here directly against ui's own compiled dist/tokens/contrast-cli.js, the same way check:package-governance below invokes governance's own dist/cli.js, rather than via `npx` or a workspace script indirection. Needs `npm run build` (ui's own `dist/` is gitignored) to have run first, same as check:package-governance.
scripts.//check-neutrality: The structural half of publish safety, for material meant to be shared between parties who do not govern each other: an absolute path or a named home directory discloses one operator's machine layout without containing a single denylisted string, so check:safety can never see it. Runs the BUILT @vespeneventures/conventions scan rather than a second copy of those regexes here — hence its position after build, alongside check:package-governance and check:contrast.
scripts.//check-release-readiness: Did a package's shipped content change since its version last did, scoped to the diff against origin/main (or local main)? Offline and hermetic (see scripts/check-release-readiness.test.mjs) — no network call, just local git refs — but deliberately NOT part of `check` below: its answer is only as fresh as the contributor's local origin/main, which `git fetch` keeps current but `check`'s other gates never depend on being current for anything. Run explicitly, or trust CI's `release-readiness` job, which passes the pull request's real base explicitly rather than relying on a local ref at all. A separate `--audit` mode also exists for whole-repo, non-diff-scoped investigation — see the script's own header for why that mode is a heuristic and is not run in CI.
scripts.//check-builds-first: build runs before typecheck for the same reason ci.yml does it in that order: dist/ is gitignored, so on a fresh clone a package's internal dependency has no .d.ts until it has been compiled. Without this a contributor's first `npm run check` fails on a clean checkout even though nothing is wrong.
scripts.check: npm run check:root-entry && npm run check:scope && npm run check:registry && npm run check:workspace-links && npm run check:gates && npm run check:safety && npm run check:readme && npm run check:contamination && npm run check:typechecked-assertions && npm run build && npm run check:package-governance && npm run check:contrast && npm run check:neutrality && npm run typecheck && npm run test
scripts.//preflight: Everything a package must pass before a publish is even proposed. Unlike `check`, this scans the packed TARBALL and asks the registry whether the name is already taken.
scripts.//check-conversation: Deliberately NOT part of `check` above. Every other check gate scans this checkout — offline, hermetic, exactly reproducible on a fork's CI run with no credentials. This one scans GitHub's live API instead: it needs network access and an authenticated `gh`, neither of which a fork's CI or an offline run has, so wiring it into `check` would make the whole chain fail (or silently no-op) for every contributor who isn't the repository owner. Run it separately, where those preconditions are actually met.
scripts.//check-conversation-draft: The prevention mode: scan text BEFORE it is posted to an issue or PR, while withholding it is still free. Pass --file <path>, or pipe the draft text in: `echo "..." | npm run check:conversation:draft --`.
